brief: Weekly recap from GS's US industrials/materials analyst: industrials rose 40bps last week, underperforming the broader market, while materials fell about 40bps. Individual movers had mixed drivers: FLY, RKLB, BETA and YSS led gains with no clear explanation; AAON (+16%) followed a sell-side company visit; ESAB (+11%) rose as Middle East fears eased; QXO (+9%) benefited as rates came off multi-decade highs. Decliners included VOYG (convertible offering), CF, SMID cyclicals OSK/DAN/DCH, and FTAI (-8% on a Q3 estimate cut). GS expects industrial seasonality to improve into year-end but sees more downside than upside risk to the coming ISM print versus consensus (55.2 from 54.6). Prime brokerage data show broad de-grossing, with Industrials among the most net-sold global sectors this week even though the book stays overweight the sector versus MSCI World. Previews: ALK's investor day should remove its already-doubted $10 2027 EPS target; CCL's preview is near-term cautious but sees unappreciated long-term PROPEL upside; AYI looks priced for an in-line guide.
